job.style: a step-by-step explanation of a process

response.passage: When a sports injury occurs, immediate action is vital to prevent further damage. If you suspect a sprain or strain, the RICE method is the gold standard for initial care. First, Rest the injured area immediately to avoid stressing the tissues. Second, Ice the area using a cold pack for 15-20 minutes to reduce swelling, but never apply direct heat, as heat increases blood flow and worsens inflammation. Third, Compress the injury with an elastic bandage, ensuring it is snug but not so tight that it cuts off circulation. Finally, Elevate the limb above the level of your heart to help fluid drain away from the injury site. It is a common myth that you can 'walk off' an injury or that pain disappearing means you are fully healed. In reality, pain is a warning signal, and returning to play before a doctor clears you can lead to chronic issues. Even if you feel okay, a joint that has been injured is weaker than before and requires gradual rehabilitation. Furthermore, if you experience a blow to the head, you must stop playing immediately, even if you feel fine, because concussion symptoms can be delayed. Never assume that the absence of immediate pain or visible deformity means an injury is minor; always prioritize rest and professional medical advice over returning to the game.
response.summary: The RICE method provides essential first aid for sports injuries by managing swelling and preventing further damage. Always prioritize rest and professional medical evaluation over the urge to return to play quickly.
